_comments: SALES' TWO TASK TYPES, SEEDED FROM SALES INTO ANOTHER APP'S TABLE.
This is the only directory here whose `entity` belongs to a different app, so it is worth saying
why rather than leaving a reader to assume it is a mistake. Amith's ruling, 2026-08-20: 'I will
create a more robust task type table in Tasks for you. But the metadata rows for these task types
will be created by the sales open app.' Tasks owns the SHAPE; the app that raises a kind of task
owns the ROW. bizapps-tasks seeds only the five generic types (General, Action Item, Follow-up,
Deliverable, Approval Request) and deliberately does not carry these two.
That split is the right one. A task type nobody raises is dead vocabulary, and tasks has no way to
know that closing a won deal produces exactly these two pieces of work. It also means these rows
arrive and depart with the feature that needs them: uninstall sales and its task types go with it.
WHY `Code` MATTERS HERE. bizapps-tasks PR #42 (merged 2026-08-20 14:01) added `TaskType.Code`,
NOT NULL and UNIQUE. Before it, the only stable handle on a type row was its UUID, so
`CloseWonTaskService` took the two IDs as deployment configuration on `Pipeline.CloseWonPolicy` --
every deployment restating a fact that is the same everywhere, and a fixed UUID travelling through
config to reach code that only ever wanted 'the order-review one'. `Code` retires that: the
service resolves ORDER_REVIEW and CONTRACT_PROCESSING itself, and the configuration keys go away.
SCREAMING_SNAKE, matching the five tasks already seeds (GENERAL, ACTION_ITEM, FOLLOW_UP,
DELIVERABLE, APPROVAL_REQUEST). A code is an identifier, not a label -- renaming the display Name
must never change it, which is the whole reason for having both.
FIXED UUIDs, carried over unchanged from when these rows lived in bizapps-tasks' own metadata, so
a database already holding them is UPDATED rather than given a second copy under a new ID.
PUSH ORDER: nothing in sales references these, and they reference nothing in sales. They are last
in `directoryOrder` before `applications` only for tidiness.
DEPENDENCY, AND IT IS REAL: pushing this directory requires bizapps-tasks to be installed in the
target database. `mj sync push` cannot create a row in a table that is not there, and the failure
is a plain 'entity not found' rather than anything that explains itself. Sales runs standalone by
design, so a deployment without tasks simply does not push this directory -- and
`CloseWonTaskService` already treats an unresolvable type as an Issue rather than a fault.

fields.Name: Order Review
fields.Description: Review the order behind a won deal, correct it if needed, then advance it. Advancing is the confirm that locks the order, books the journal entries and triggers invoicing — so this task is the control on money leaving the building, not a reminder.

_comments: Raised only when the pipeline's `CloseWonPolicy.CreateContract` flag is set -- B2B in the seeded
data, but read as a FLAG and never as a pipeline name.
The description carries the steps as prose, which is a stopgap rather than a design. PR #42 also
added `TaskTypeStatus`, a per-type lifecycle with Sequence, IsDefault, IsTerminal and MacroStatus,
and that is a better home for them -- see D-13 in DECISIONS-NEEDED.md. Left as prose here because
seeding statuses commits sales to a workflow shape that finance has not confirmed, and a wrong
lifecycle is harder to walk back than a wrong paragraph.

fields.Name: Contract Processing
fields.Description: Process the contract a won deal created: attach the executed document, confirm the agreement version against what it cites, record the executed/effective/end dates, validate whether the template was modified, and move the contract to active.
